name: Chari Dance

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A knowledgeable cultural historian or a member of the Gurjar community.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

This is Chari Dance. Traditional.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the desert state of Rajasthan, specifically the Ajmer and Kishangarh regions.
It celebrates the lifelong ritual of women collecting water for their families.
on_screen: Map: India · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed at marriage celebrations, the birth of a male child, and at festivals of goodness.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Chari Folk Dance of Rajasthan.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0d/Chari_Folk_Dance_of_Rajasthan.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by a group of women who balance lit earthenware or brass pots on their heads.
Dancers execute graceful limb movements and deep knee swirls while keeping the flaming pots balanced without touching them.
Watch for Chari Balancing.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Group dance, moving quietly around the floor.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is played using the Nagada, Dholak, Dhol, Harmonium, Thali, and Bankia.
The Bankia is the most common instrument and is known for its powerful, eerie sound.
Listen for the Nagada, Dholak, Dhol, Harmonium.
The music is characterized by the powerful and eerie sound of the Bankia, supported by percussion instruments like the Nagada and Dholak.

images.description: This media has been taken in the country: India

Because water is scarce in the desert region of Rajasthan, women must journey for miles to fetch water, carrying pitchers atop their heads. This dance captures the delight of embarking on this journey and maintaining balance with the water pot.
